items.title: 66096_Monk Montgomery oral history interview
items.q: Gee whiz, will you look at that, I can't think of his name — anyway, he had a steady job. I'll get his name; I got a record by him in there.

ctx.x: This was before Wes really took off, right?

Yeah. And he was saying, because...Plus that his wife and even the kids weren't happy about that part of the country. Everybody wanted to go home. And when we were out on the road, we stayed so long trying to make some money, that it kept him away from home. It kept us all away, but a guy with a bigger family gets affected more. And he was no two ways about it; nothing to do with the music, nothing to do with us personally. He had to go.

Because his family was unhappy and he was too, because he wasn't making anything. So there was no question about that. He did what he had to do. So he went home. And that sortof brought the Montgomery Brothers to a dead end.

items.title: 66096_Monk Montgomery oral history interview
items.q: Curtis Amy! He had a little quintet. He said, 'We're steady, man, it's a group. Why don't you come on down, man? It would be great.' ... Anyhow, I came down for the job with Curtis Amy.

ctx.x: I went to Los Angeles. Howard Roberts had a record date, and I went to make the record date and while I was there, I went over that Sunday night to a...I can't think of the name of this club, down on Adams...and a tenor player was working there by the name of...Gee whiz, will you look at that, I can't

think of his name — anyway, he had a steady job. I'll get his name; I got a record by him in there. And I went by and sat in. And he said, 'Man, are you in town? Are you...?' He had some kid playing bass. He was telling me on the break, 'Man, I could sure use a bass player. This kid don't know all the tunes and ...' blah blah blah blah. And I said, well, I had moved down but I'm trying to think about it. 'Oh, man, I'll get it straight with the union and we could take care of business, because if I don't have…

So I thought about it, because you know, for me, a six night a week gig, that's better than digging swimming pools. Anyhow, I came down for the job with Curtis Amy. After I was down for a couple of weeks, I brought my family down to Los Angeles. That was her home anyhow, and it was very easy to get comfortable right there.
